title: U.S. Senate · Delaware

context.text: Incumbent Chris Coons (D) won the September 15, 2026 Democratic primary with 78% of the vote. Michael Katz, a physician and former Delaware state senator, won the Republican primary with 77.3%. Travis Stevens is running as a write-in candidate unaffiliated with either major party.

candidates.name: Chris Coons

summary.text: Chris Coons is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election. A Delaware lawyer and former manufacturing-company employee, he served on and then led New Castle County government before being elected to the U.S. Senate in 2010. He sits on the Appropriations, Foreign Relations, Judiciary, Small Business and Ethics committees and is running on his Senate record.

background.text: Born in Greenwich, Connecticut, in 1963. According to his Senate website, he was raised in Hockessin, Delaware.

Earned a bachelor's degree in chemistry and political science from Amherst College (1985), spent a semester at the University of Nairobi in Kenya, and later earned an M.A.R. from Yale Divinity School and a J.D. from Yale Law School (both 1992).

After college he worked with the South African Council of Churches in the anti-apartheid movement. As a law student he founded the Delaware chapter of the national "I Have a Dream" Foundation, and he later launched and ran the foundation's AmeriCorps program, according to his Senate website.
Worked for Delaware-based W.L. Gore & Associates before entering county government; Ballotpedia also describes him as a nonprofit executive and attorney.
Served as president of the New Castle County Council (2001-2005) and as New Castle County Executive (2005-2010).

Elected to the U.S. Senate in 2010 and has served since. His Senate site lists committee service on Appropriations, Foreign Relations, Judiciary, Small Business and Entrepreneurship, and Ethics; he is Vice Chair of the Ethics Committee and the ranking Democrat on the Defense Appropriations subcommittee.

According to his Senate website, he was an ordained elder in the Presbyterian Church and is one of three senators with a divinity degree. He lives in Wilmington with his wife, Annie; they have three grown children.

positions.summary: His Senate issues page says he is working to protect and strengthen Medicaid, Medicare and the Affordable Care Act, and to make expanded ACA marketplace tax credits permanent.
positions.quote: protecting and strengthening the programs that give people a health care lifeline: Medicaid, Medicare, and the Affordable Care Act

positions.summary: His Senate issues page says he is fighting to restore and protect reproductive freedom, including access to abortion, and supports the Reproductive Freedom for Women Act, which would put the protections of Roe v. Wade into federal law.
positions.quote: He is fighting to restore and protect reproductive freedom including access to abortion, birth control, and fertility treatments

positions.summary: In a February 2026 statement on the Supreme Court's tariff ruling, he criticized the administration's tariffs as unlawful and unwise and said they raised prices on everyday goods.
positions.quote: President Trump’s arbitrary tariff regime is as unlawful as it is unwise.

positions.summary: In an April 2026 statement, he said he voted to end the Iran war under a War Powers Resolution, and called the war one waged without a publicly stated rationale, strategy or goal.
positions.quote: I just voted once again to end President Trump’s war of choice with Iran

positions.summary: Introduced the PUBLIC SAFETY Act in January 2026 with Sen. Cortez Masto, which would redirect almost $75 billion in ICE funding from the 2025 reconciliation law to local law enforcement programs.
positions.quote: introduced the PUBLIC SAFETY Act to redirect almost $75 billion in funding passed in the Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) from Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)

record.text: Serves as Vice Chairman of the Senate Select Committee on Ethics and is a member of the Judiciary Committee, Foreign Relations Committee, Appropriations Committee (Ranking Member, Defense Subcommittee), and Small Business and Entrepreneurship Committee in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Michael Katz

summary.text: Michael (Mike) Katz is the Republican nominee. He is a pediatric critical care anesthesiologist and business owner who served one term in the Delaware State Senate (2009-2013) as a Democrat, ran for U.S. Senate in 2024 as an Independent, and later registered as a Republican. He says he is running on lowering the cost of living, health care reform, term limits and fiscal accountability.

background.text: According to his Ballotpedia survey response, he grew up in a working-class family and was the first man in his family to attend college.
Earned a medical degree and an MBA in international business from Georgetown University.

Came to Delaware in 1996 when he was recruited from Boston Children's Hospital to A.I. duPont Hospital for Children, according to his campaign website; he has practiced as a pediatric critical care anesthesiologist in Delaware for over 20 years.

Is a business owner; WHYY reports he owns a commercial real estate company. His campaign website says he has held leadership roles with the Medical Society of Delaware and the American Medical Association.
Elected as a Democrat to Delaware State Senate District 4 (north of Wilmington, including Greenville, Centreville and Hockessin), serving 2009 to 2013.
In the State Senate he worked on legislation about lobbying reform, term limits and health care policy; his campaign website also cites the creation of the Delaware Health Information Network.
Ran for U.S. Senate in 2024 as an Independent for the seat vacated by Tom Carper, losing to Lisa Blunt Rochester.
Won the September 15, 2026 Republican primary over John Shulli. He lives in Delaware with his wife, Trish; they have three adult children, according to his campaign materials.

priorities.text: Bringing real-world medical and business problem-solving experience to the Senate.
A "Delaware first, people over party" approach, working across party lines as he says he did in the state senate.
Government accountability and reform, including congressional term limits, fiscal responsibility, and reducing the influence of special interests.

positions.summary: His campaign platform backs passing the SAVE Act and lists mandatory proof of citizenship as part of his voter integrity framework.
positions.quote: Mandatory Proof of Citizenship — Passing the SAVE Act

positions.summary: His campaign platform says he would oppose federal red-flag mandates and firearm registries.
positions.quote: I will oppose any federal red-flag mandates, firearm registries, or unconstitutional restrictions

positions.summary: His campaign platform says he would support policies that restrict women's sports competition to female athletes, which would exclude transgender women.
positions.quote: I will support policies that preserve women's sports as a competitive category for biological females

record.text: Served as a member of the Delaware State Senate before running for U.S. Senate.
Sponsored and passed SB 241 (146th General Assembly), establishing the Brandywine Valley National Scenic Byway Advisory Board to oversee preservation of the byway corridor.
Sponsored Senate Resolution No. 14, expressing the Senate's intent to stream live audio of its sessions.

candidates.researchNotes: Delaware's official roll-call vote records for the Delaware General Assembly (legis.delaware.gov) are rendered via JavaScript and could not be retrieved directly after repeated attempts; the two record items above are drawn from official bill-text PDFs on legis.delaware.gov (confirming sponsorship and passage), supplementing his campaign site's self-reported legislative record.

candidates.name: Travis Stevens

summary.text: Travis Jack Stevens is an unaffiliated write-in candidate. He is a nurse and massage therapist who lives near Rehoboth Beach and describes his campaign as people-funded, built around daily public letters to Delaware voters.

background.text: According to his Ballotpedia survey response, he was born in Hagerstown, Maryland, to a working-class family.

Worked for years as a nurse, including four years as a travel ICU nurse (three at David Grant Medical Center, a Department of Defense hospital on Travis Air Force Base), and worked in a COVID unit in Delaware during the pandemic, per his survey response.
Currently works as a massage therapist, lives near Rehoboth Beach, and sings with the CAMP Rehoboth Chorus, per his survey response.
Publishes a series of daily public letters to Delaware voters at travisjackstevens.com covering healthcare, foreign policy, housing, and democratic reform.

priorities.text: Universal healthcare access and lower prescription drug prices.
Expanded housing supply and affordability measures statewide.
Campaign finance reform and ranked-choice voting; says he accepts no Super PAC money.

positions.summary: Supports universal healthcare access and opposes pharmaceutical industry pricing practices.
Supports expanded housing supply and affordability measures statewide.
Says Congress, not the president, decides when the country goes to war.
positions.quote: Under the Constitution, Congress decides when this country goes to war, not the president.

candidates.researchNotes: Stevens has also stated opposition to U.S. military involvement in the Iran war and has criticized U.S. policy toward the conflict in Gaza, citing International Court of Justice findings, per his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. Added statements and a war-powers position from the Platform page of his campaign website (travisjackstevens.com/platform).

statements.quote: The wealthiest Americans and the biggest corporations pay their fair share, and that pays for health care, housing and education for everyone.
statements.context: On his campaign website's Platform page

statements.quote: I'll vote to stop sending weapons that kill civilians in Gaza. American tax dollars must not fund the killing of civilians.
statements.context: On his campaign website's Platform page

statements.quote: A home for everyone. That means investing in affordable housing, protecting tenants and closing corporate landlord loopholes.
statements.context: On his campaign website's Platform page
